CELLULA / MODEL v0.6

A small model of a living system.

A generic mammalian eukaryotic cell with a clamped extracellular bath, a fixed adenylate pool, passive ion leaks, an ATP-driven sodium–potassium pump, a spherical elastic surface, gated ion pores, and water channels.

This is an educational model with illustrative parameters, not a calibrated prediction of a particular cell. The nucleus, ER, and Golgi are visual context. Spatial particles and color overlays illustrate calculated bulk values; they are not molecular trajectories or resolved concentration fields.

What is connected?

Glucose and oxygen support ATP production. ATP powers the Na⁺/K⁺ pump (3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in per ATP). Passive ion currents and pumping set a quasi-steady membrane voltage. Ion amounts set osmolarity, water changes volume, and volume changes all internal concentrations.

State variables & units

The solver tracks Na⁺, K⁺, Cl⁻, cytosolic and matrix ATP amounts, mitochondrial potential, relative pore opening, and volume using fourth-order Runge–Kutta with a maximum 0.04 s step. Amounts use mM × V₀; concentrations divide by V/V₀. V₀ is a 10 µm radius sphere (4.19 pL). The combined cytosolic and matrix ATP + ADP amount is fixed at 5 mM × V₀. A fixed, singly negative impermeant pool closes bulk charge and osmotic balance.

Physics: ion currents & water

Eᵢ = RT / (zᵢF) · ln(cᵢ,out / cᵢ,in)
Vₘ = (gNa ENa + gK EK + gCl ECl − P) / Σg
Jᵢ = gᵢ(Vₘ − Eᵢ)
dnNa/dt = −JNa − 3P
dnK/dt = −JK + 2P ·   dnCl/dt = JCl
dV/dt = 0.18 Lw A(ΔΠ − ΔPelastic) / (RT × 300 / 1000)
ΔΠ = RT(Cin − Cout) / 1000   [kPa]

Currents use equivalent mM × V₀/s; conductances use equivalent mM × V₀/(mV·s). The Cl⁻ flux sign follows its negative charge. A = (V/V₀)²ᐟ³; volume rate is in V₀/s. Osmolarities in mOsm/L are numerically mol/m³ for pressure in Pa; the dashboard displays kPa. Electrical relaxation is assumed instantaneous: no action potentials or membrane capacitance are solved. Lw is relative water permeability. Pressure in the water equation is in kPa; tension-derived elastic pressure opposes osmotic inflow.

Surface mechanics, bending & pores

εA = max(0, (V/V₀)²ᐟ³/(1+reserve/100) − 1)
σ = KA εA ·   ΔPelastic = 2σ / radius
target = manual + (1 − manual) · stretchGate · σ²/(2² + σ²)
d(open)/dt = (target − open) / 0.8 s
gpore = 0.006 A Qleak · open
gᵢ = gᵢ,base + gᵢ,pore
ripple = Rcell / √(1680 κ/kBT + 40 σRcell²/kBT)

KA and σ use mN/m; radius uses µm in the Laplace equation, giving kPa. KA is an illustrative effective surface modulus, not a measured whole-cell rigidity or a fit for a lipid bilayer. The shell carries no compressive tension. A configurable area reserve is recruited before elastic stretching; it is a simple geometric allowance, not membrane trafficking. The bending control is κ in kBT at the current temperature. The ripple readout is the equipartition coefficient for one l = 6 spherical mode (40 × 42 = 1680), not total RMS displacement. It affects visible membrane undulations; it does not add a bending force to the spherical volume equation. Periodic animation displays this scale at 3×, rather than solving stochastic trajectories.

Manual pore opening sets a population target, with a 0.8 s relaxation time. Stretch-sensitive gating adds an illustrative Hill response with half-activation at 2 mN/m. Broad pores conduct Na⁺, K⁺ and Cl⁻; selective modes add only Na⁺ or K⁺ conductance. The population conductance and gating curve are chosen for exploration, not calibrated channel kinetics or physical pore radii. Water permeability is a separate multiplier: higher permeability changes the speed of water transport, not the equilibrium pressure balance. Ion flows, passive and pump contributions, are positive inward in the transport table. No internal fluid velocity field or Navier–Stokes flow is solved.

Large area expansion and high tension can exceed what a lipid bilayer tolerates. The current effective shell has no rupture, pore nucleation, dynamic membrane trafficking, cortex, or repair model; do not interpret such states as intact-cell predictions.

Compartmental mammalian energetics — v0.3

This is a new reduced module inspired by chemiosmotic energy coupling, not an implementation or reproduction of Beard (2005). All kinetic coefficients below are illustrative. The cytosol occupies 90% and the mitochondrial matrix 10% of model volume; both fractions remain fixed during swelling. Plasma-membrane ion concentrations still use effective whole-cell volume, an explicit coarse-graining approximation. The two adenylate pools contain 4.5 and 0.5 mM × V₀ respectively; ATP and ADP exchange in opposite directions with equal flux.

Vc = 0.9 V · Vm = 0.1 V
G = glucose/(1+glucose) · O = oxygen/(0.01+oxygen)
D = ADPc/(0.5+ADPc) · q = 2^((T−37)/10)
Jgly = 0.1 G D q [1+2(1−O)]
Resp = (G/(5/6)) (O/(0.2/0.21)) capacity (1−ψ/220)/(1−150/220) q
Jsyn = (4/9) [ADPm/(0.5+ADPm)]/(2/3) max(0,(ψ−60)/90) q V
Jexchange = (20/9) exchange (ATPm_amount/0.5 − ATPc_amount/4.5) V
dψ/dt = 30 [Resp − 0.85 Jsyn/((4/9)V) − 0.15 leak ψ/150]
Juse = 0.5390653 demand q [ATPc/(0.3+ATPc)]/(3/3.3)
dATPc_amount/dt = (Jgly−Juse) Vc + Jexchange − P
dATPm_amount/dt = Jsyn − Jexchange

ψ is the positive magnitude of the matrix-negative potential in mV; the dashboard shows its negative sign. Jsyn and Jexchange use mM × V₀/s, while Jgly and Juse use cytosolic mM/s. Capacity is respiratory capacity/100. Resp is a dimensionless drive proxy, not a measured oxygen-consumption rate. The exchange law is phenomenological, not a thermodynamic ANT model. The electrical equation is an effective energy-storage relaxation law; mitochondrial charge and free-energy conservation are not explicitly resolved. Negative exchange returns ATP to mitochondria. The fixed matrix adenylate pool and fixed compartment proportions are assumptions.

Glucose and oxygen remain clamped substrate proxies. pH, proton counts, NADH, phosphate, finite extracellular depletion, and respiratory complexes are future additions. The reference is chosen to balance at cytosolic ATP 3 mM, matrix ATP 4 mM, and ψ = 150 mV.

Evidence and validation status

Implemented and numerically checked: plasma-membrane bulk charge balance, bounded adenylate pools, equal-and-opposite ATP/ADP exchange, reference stability, perturbation direction, and timestep convergence. Literature-informed: pump–leak architecture, osmotic transport, membrane fluctuation scaling, compartmental chemiosmotic coupling. Not yet demonstrated: reproduction of published experimental curves, fitted cell-type parameters, quantitative predictive accuracy, or a full thermodynamic mitochondrial model.

Candidate reference implementations: Beard (2005), mitochondrial bioenergetics; thermodynamically consistent Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase; Jiang & Sun (2013), cortex, pressure and volume. These are development targets, not claims that their complete models have been incorporated.

Biology: the ATP-driven pump

P = 0.025 A q (1 − blockade/100) · fATP · fNa · fK
fATP = ([ATP]/(1+[ATP])) / (3/4)
fNa = ([Na]³/(10³+[Na]³)) / (15³/(10³+15³))
fK = (Kout/(1+Kout)) / (5/6)

P uses mM × V₀/s. Pump activity is shown relative to the reference pump at the same temperature and surface area. “ATP-supported activity” is an illustrative proxy: 100 · fATP · exp(−1.5(V/V₀−1)²). It is not viability, gene expression, or a measured synthesis rate.

Reference parameters

Bath Na⁺ = 150 × osmolarity/300 − Kout; Cl⁻ = 145 × osmolarity/300. Omitted bath counterions supply the remaining charge balance. K⁺ replaces Na⁺ at fixed total cation concentration. Leak conductances scale with area and Q₁₀ = 1.3; metabolic and pump rates use Q₁₀ = 2. Conductances are chosen so the reference ion state has Vₘ = −70 mV.

Limits & next steps

No cell wall, signaling network, gene regulation, calcium, pH, alternative fuels, full membrane shape mechanics, resolved fluid dynamics, or death model. Organelles are schematic and enlarged. Temperature only changes rate factors and Nernst potentials; heat injury is omitted. The run stops outside V/V₀ = 0.45–1.8 or the positive-amount domain. Long-term adaptation is not modeled.

Next milestones are reproduction of published benchmarks, a proton/pH module, calcium signaling, full cortex/shape mechanics, and calibration to a particular mammalian cell type.

Scientific foundations

The pump-leak structure is adapted at a conceptual level from Kay (2017), How Cells Can Control Their Size by Pumping Ions. Membrane fluctuations are informed by Curvature fluctuations of fluid vesicles reveal hydrodynamic dissipation within the bilayer. Stretch-gating is inspired by Guharay & Sachs (1984). Our elastic shell, energy module, pore population, and gating coefficients are reduced illustrative models, not reproductions or calibrated fits of these papers. Background: Cooper, The Cell: Metabolic Energy.
